1	# obsd
2	
3	Minimal, dependency-free backend skeleton for **metrics ingestion, alerting and
4	SLO tracking**. Python 3.10+, standard library only, offline, deterministic
5	(every time-dependent entry point takes an injected `now_ms`).
6	
7	The lane goal is a metrics collection, alerting and SLO backend that grows
8	towards time-series writes and downsampling, label indexing and a query subset,
9	aggregation and sliding windows, alert rules with silencing and inhibition,
10	notification routing and dedup, SLO and error-budget math, retention and
11	compaction, multi-tenant quota, access control and audit, and consistent reads
12	under high availability. This seed implements the first, smallest *real* slice of
13	each of those areas.
14	
15	## Run
16	
17	```bash
18	# HTTP API (data dir flag is global and comes BEFORE the subcommand)
19	python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
20	
21	# test suite
22	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	Both commands are run offline with the system interpreter; no third-party
26	package is imported anywhere.
27	
28	## CLI
29	
30	`python3 -m obsd [--data-dir ./obsd_data] <command> ...` prints exactly one line
31	of JSON on stdout. On error it prints one line of JSON (`{"error":"..."}`) on
32	stderr and exits non-zero.
33	
34	| Command | Example |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `serve` | `python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080` |
37	| `quota-set` | `python3 -m obsd quota-set --tenant acme --max-series 1000 --max-points 1000000` |
38	| `quota-get` | `python3 -m obsd quota-get --tenant acme` |
39	| `retention-set` | `python3 -m obsd retention-set --tenant acme --retention-ms 86400000` (omit `--retention-ms` for no cleanup) |
40	| `retention-get` | `python3 -m obsd retention-get --tenant acme` |
41	| `retention-run` | `python3 -m obsd retention-run --now-ms 2000 [--tenant acme] [--dry-run] [--return-revision]` |
42	| `downsampling-set` | `python3 -m obsd downsampling-set --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --step-ms 60000 --agg sum --agg avg` |
43	| `downsampling-get` | `python3 -m obsd downsampling-get --tenant acme --metric latency_ms` |
44	| `downsampling-run` | `python3 -m obsd downsampling-run --now-ms 2000 [--tenant acme] [--metric latency_ms] [--dry-run] [--return-revision]` |
45	| `downsampled-query` | `python3 -m obsd downsampled-query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --agg avg [--read-token T]` |
46	| `consistency-token` | `python3 -m obsd consistency-token --tenant acme` |
47	| `write` | `python3 -m obsd write --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --label host=a --sample 1000:12.5 --now-ms 2000 [--return-revision]` |
48	| `write-batch` | `python3 -m obsd write-batch --entries '[{"tenant":"acme","metric":"latency_ms","samples":[[1000,12.5]]}]' --now-ms 2000 [--return-revision]` |
49	| `query` | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --agg avg [--read-token T]` |
50	| `query` (grouped) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --agg avg --group-by '["host"]'` |
51	| `query` (matchers) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --matchers '[{"key":"host","op":"=~","value":"api-.*"}]'` |
52	| `query` (sliding window) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --window-ms 5000 --agg avg` |
53	| `export` | `python3 -m obsd export --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 [--read-token T]` |
54	| `replay` | `python3 -m obsd replay --snapshot '{"version":1,"snapshot_id":"...","entries":[...]}' --now-ms 5000 [--return-revision]` |
55	| `rule-add` | `python3 -m obsd rule-add --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --comparator "<" --threshold 10 --window-ms 60000 --for-ms 30000 --agg avg --severity warning` |
56	| `eval` | `python3 -m obsd eval --now-ms 68000` |
57	| `alerts` | `python3 -m obsd alerts --tenant acme --state firing` |
58	| `silence-add` | `python3 -m obsd silence-add --tenant acme --starts-ms 0 --ends-ms 90000 --reason maintenance` |
59	| `route-add` | `python3 -m obsd route-add --tenant acme --target pager --label host=a --severity critical --event firing --repeat-ms 300000` |
60	| `route-list` | `python3 -m obsd route-list --tenant acme` |
61	| `notification-list` | `python3 -m obsd notification-list --tenant acme --acked false` |
62	| `notification-ack` | `python3 -m obsd notification-ack --id notification-00001` |
63	| `slo set` | `python3 -m obsd slo set --tenant acme --name availability --metric latency_ms --good-comparator ">=" --threshold 1 --target-ratio 0.9 --window-ms 60000` |
64	| `slo status` | `python3 -m obsd slo status --name availability --now-ms 60000 [--read-token T]` |
65	| `principal-create` | `python3 -m obsd principal-create --id ops --token s3cret --role admin --tenant acme --tenant globex` |
66	| `principal-list` | `python3 -m obsd principal-list` |
67	| `principal-revoke` | `python3 -m obsd principal-revoke --id ops` |
68	
69	## HTTP API
70	
71	Errors are always JSON: `{"error":"..."}` with status 400 (bad request,
72	including `invalid read token`), 404 (unknown resource) or 409 (write
73	conflict, quota exceeded or `read revision unavailable`).
74	
75	| Method | Path | Request | Response |
76	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
77	| GET | `/healthz` | – | `200 {"ok":true}` |
78	| GET | `/v1/consistency-token` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","token","revision"}` — mints a read-consistency token for the tenant |
79	| POST | `/v1/series` | `{"tenant","metric","labels","samples":[[ts,value],...],"now_ms"?,"overwrite"?,"return_revision"?}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"series_id":"..."}` (plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true), `400` on malformed input or a non-boolean `now_ms`/`overwrite`/`return_revision` (an explicit `null` `overwrite`/`return_revision` is rejected, not treated as `false`), `409` on conflicting timestamp or quota exceeded |
80	| POST | `/v1/series/batch` | `{"entries":[{"tenant","metric","samples","labels"?},...],"now_ms"?,"overwrite"?,"return_revision"?}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"results":[{"series_id","written","duplicates"},...]}` (plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true), `400` on malformed entries, `409` on conflict or quota exceeded |
81	| GET | `/v1/query` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&step=&agg=&group_by=&window=&matchers=&read_token=` (group_by and matchers are JSON arrays; matchers holds `{"key","op","value"}` objects) | `200 {"series":[{"labels":{...},"points":[[ts,value\|null],...]}]}`, `400` on an invalid read token, `409` while the token's revision is unavailable |
82	| GET | `/v1/export` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&matchers=&read_token=` (same filters and closed-interval semantics as `/v1/query`) | `200 {"version":1,"snapshot_id":"...","entries":[{"tenant","metric","labels","samples"},...]}`, `400`/`409` on read-token failures |
83	| POST | `/v1/replay` | `{"version":1,"snapshot_id":"...","entries":[...],"now_ms"?,"overwrite"?,"dry_run"?,"return_revision"?}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"results":[...],"applied":true}` (`200` with `"applied":false` for a dry run; plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true), `400` on invalid input or digest mismatch, `409` on conflict or quota exceeded |
84	| POST | `/v1/quotas` | `{"tenant","max_series":n\|null,"max_points":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/limits give `400` and leave config untouched |
85	| GET | `/v1/quotas` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports `null` limits and real usage) |
86	| POST | `/v1/retention/policies` | `{"tenant","retention_ms":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","retention_ms","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/policy or unknown fields give `400` and leave config untouched |
87	| GET | `/v1/retention/policies` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","retention_ms","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports a `null` policy and real usage) |
88	| POST | `/v1/retention/run` | `{"now_ms":n,"tenant"?,"dry_run"?,"return_revision"?}` | `200 {"dry_run":b,"tenants":[{"tenant","cutoff_ms","dropped","affected_series","remaining_points","compacted_series"},...]}` (plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true); missing/non-integer `now_ms`, non-boolean `dry_run`/`return_revision` or unknown fields give `400` |
89	| POST | `/v1/downsampling/policies` | `{"tenant","metric","step_ms":n,"aggregations":["sum",...]}` | `200 {"tenant","metric","step_ms","aggregations"}` — creates or replaces the policy (replacement keeps raw samples, clears old results); any invalid field or unknown key gives `400 {"error":"downsampling policy invalid"}` |
90	| GET | `/v1/downsampling/policies` | `?tenant=&metric=` | `200 {"tenant","metric","step_ms","aggregations"}` (unconfigured policy reports `null` fields) |
91	| POST | `/v1/downsampling/run` | `{"now_ms":n,"tenant"?,"metric"?,"dry_run"?,"return_revision"?}` | `200 {"dry_run":b,"policies":[{"tenant","metric","buckets","changed"},...]}` (plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true); any invalid argument gives `400 {"error":"downsampling run invalid"}` |
92	| GET | `/v1/query/downsampled` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&matchers=&start=&end=&agg=&read_token=` (step fixed by the policy) | `200 {"series":[{"labels":{...},"points":[[ts,value\|null],...]}]}`, `404 {"error":"downsampling policy unavailable"}` with no policy, `400 {"error":"downsampling aggregation unavailable"}` for an undeclared `agg`, `400 {"error":"downsampled query unsupported"}` for windows/grouping/counter aggregates, `400`/`409` on read-token failures |
93	| POST | `/v1/rules` | rule object | `201` stored rule |
94	| GET | `/v1/rules` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"rules":[...]}` |
95	| POST | `/v1/evaluate` | `{"now_ms":n}` | `200 {"firing":[...],"silenced":[...],"inhibited":[...],"resolved":[...]}` |
96	| GET | `/v1/alerts` | `?tenant=&state=` | `200 {"alerts":[...]}` |
97	| POST | `/v1/silences` | `{"tenant","labels","starts_ms","ends_ms","reason"}` | `201` stored silence |
98	| POST | `/v1/inhibitions` | `{"source_severity","target_severity","same_labels"?}` | `201` stored inhibition; `same_labels` must be a real boolean (omitted defaults to `true`; `null`, numbers and strings are rejected with `400` and change nothing) |
99	| POST | `/v1/notification-routes` | `{"tenant","target","labels"?,"severities"?,"events"?,"repeat_ms"?,"id"?}` | `201` stored route; `400` invalid, `409` duplicate id |
100	| GET | `/v1/notification-routes` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"routes":[...]}` |
101	| DELETE | `/v1/notification-routes/{id}` | – | `200 {"deleted":id}`; `404` unknown route (notifications are kept) |
102	| GET | `/v1/notifications` | `?tenant=&route_id=&alert_id=&acked=` | `200 {"notifications":[...]}` (read-only, never consumes) |
103	| POST | `/v1/notifications/{id}/ack` | – | `200` stored notification (re-ack returns the same record); `404` unknown notification |
104	| POST | `/v1/slos` | `{"tenant","name","metric","labels","good_comparator","threshold","target_ratio","window_ms"}` | `201` stored SLO |
105	| GET | `/v1/slos/status` | `?tenant=&name=&now_ms=&read_token=` | `200` SLO status object, `400`/`409` on read-token failures |
106	| GET | `/v1/stats` | – | `200 {"store":{...},"alerts":n}` |
107	| GET | `/v1/audit` | `?tenant=&principal_id=&outcome=&after_seq=&limit=` | `200 {"entries":[{"seq","principal_id","method","path","tenant","outcome","status"},...]}` ascending by `seq` (admin only) |
108	
109	**Access control and audit.** Principals are managed locally through the CLI
110	(`principal-create`/`principal-list`/`principal-revoke`); a principal is a
111	unique `--id`, a non-empty `--token`, a `--role` of `viewer`, `writer` or
112	`admin`, and at least one `--tenant` scope. Only the token's SHA-256 digest is
113	persisted (`access.json`); the token itself never appears in any output,
114	listing or audit record. A duplicate id is a conflict (`409` semantics), an
115	unknown id on revoke is `unknown principal: ...` (`404` semantics). While no
116	`access.json` exists, access control is off: every request stays anonymous,
117	nothing returns `401`/`403`, no audit records are written and `/healthz` is
118	always public either way.
119	
120	Once the config exists, every non-`/healthz` request must carry
121	`Authorization: Bearer <token>`: a missing, malformed or unknown token gets
122	`401 {"error":"unauthorized"}`. An authenticated principal whose role or
123	tenant scope does not cover the request gets `403 {"error":"forbidden"}`.
124	`viewer` reads resources inside its tenant scope; `writer` additionally
125	writes series, manages rules, silences, routes and SLOs and acknowledges
126	notifications inside its scope; `admin` additionally runs quotas, inhibitions,
127	evaluation, stats and the audit endpoint, and is the only role allowed to run
128	cross-tenant operations (requests with no single tenant, such as an
129	unfiltered `GET /v1/alerts`). Batch writes are checked per entry: if any
130	entry's tenant is outside the caller's scope the whole batch is rejected with
131	`403` before anything is written, preserving atomicity. Principals created or
132	revoked through the CLI take effect on a running server without a restart.
133	
134	Every non-`/healthz` request — authentication rejections, authorization
135	denials and business failures included — appends one persistent audit record
136	to `audit.jsonl` with a monotonically increasing `seq`:
137	`{"seq","principal_id","method","path","tenant","outcome","status"}`, where
138	`principal_id` is `null` when the request could not be authenticated,
139	`tenant` is `null` when the request has no single tenant, and `outcome` is
140	`allowed` (authorized, status < 400), `denied` (`401`/`403`) or `failed`
141	(authorized but the business logic rejected it). The log is reloaded on
142	startup, so records and the `seq` sequence survive restarts.
143	`GET /v1/audit` (admin only) filters by `tenant`, `principal_id`, `outcome`
144	and `after_seq` (entries with `seq > after_seq`) and pages with a positive
145	integer `limit`; invalid filters are `400`, non-admin access is `403`.
146	
147	## Data model
148	
149	A series identity is `(tenant, metric, sorted(label pairs))`. The canonical
150	identity string joins the tenant, the metric and every `key=value` label pair
151	(sorted by key) with `\n`:
152	
153	```
154	acme\nlatency_ms\nhost=a\nregion=eu
155	```
156	
157	`series_id = sha256(canonical_identity).hexdigest()`, so the same logical series
158	always maps to the same 64-character id, independent of label insertion order.
159	
160	Storage layout (all writes atomic via temp file + `os.replace`):
161	
162	```
163	<data-dir>/series.json              registry: series_id -> tenant/metric/labels
164	<data-dir>/points/<series_id>.jsonl one {"t":ts,"v":value} object per line
165	<data-dir>/quotas.json              tenant -> {"max_series","max_points"} limits
166	<data-dir>/retention.json           tenant -> {"retention_ms"} retention policies
167	<data-dir>/rules.json               <data-dir>/alerts.json
168	<data-dir>/slos.json                <data-dir>/silences.json
169	<data-dir>/inhibitions.json         <data-dir>/counters.json
170	<data-dir>/routes.json              <data-dir>/notifications.json
171	<data-dir>/notify_state.json        per-(route, alert) notification dedup state
172	<data-dir>/access.json              principals: id, token SHA-256 digest, role, tenants
173	<data-dir>/audit.jsonl              one audit record per line, seq monotonically increasing
174	<data-dir>/revision.json            persistent revision counter + token-signing secret
175	<data-dir>/downsampling.json        (tenant, metric) downsampling policies
176	<data-dir>/downsampled/<sid>.json   persisted downsampled buckets per series
177	```
178	
179	A directory written before quotas existed simply has no `quotas.json`, which
180	means every tenant is unlimited; limits and usage are reloaded together on
181	construction so a reopen always reports a consistent snapshot.
182	
183	`SeriesStore` and `AlertEngine` each guard their state with a
184	`threading.RLock`, so the threaded HTTP server can serve concurrent requests; all
185	state is reloaded from disk on construction, so a restart preserves series,
186	points, rules, alerts, silences, inhibitions, SLOs, notification routes and
187	queued notifications.
188	
189	## Semantics and formulas
190	
191	**Idempotent write.** `write(tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None,
192	overwrite=False)` stores `(timestamp_ms, value)` pairs. Writing an existing
193	`(series, timestamp)` with the *same* value is a duplicate: it changes nothing
194	and is counted in `duplicates`. A *different* value for a stored timestamp is a
195	conflict: it raises `ObsError` (`409` over HTTP) unless `overwrite=True`, in
196	which case the stored value is replaced and counted in `written`. A timestamp
197	greater than the injected `now` (when `now` is given) is rejected. `now` is
198	`None`/omitted (no future check) or a non-boolean integer; `overwrite` must be
199	a boolean (default `False`). Anything else raises `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP)
200	before any validation or state change: no series, points, write counter, quota
201	usage or temp file is touched.
202	
203	**Atomic multi-series write.** `write_batch(entries, now=None, overwrite=False)`
204	(also `POST /v1/series/batch` and the CLI `write-batch --entries '<json>'`)
205	applies a non-empty list of `{"tenant","metric","samples","labels"?}` entries
206	(`labels` omitted means `{}`, no other keys allowed) as one all-or-nothing
207	unit. Entries may span tenants and metrics and may repeat a series. `now` is
208	`null`/omitted (no future check) or a non-boolean integer; `overwrite` must be
209	a boolean (default `false`). The whole batch is validated before any conflict
210	is reported, and all conflicts before any quota check. Entries and their
211	samples are then applied in input order, so a later entry sees the earlier
212	entries of the same batch: a same-value restatement is a duplicate, a
213	differing value conflicts unless `overwrite` (then it replaces and counts as
214	written). The result is `{"written","duplicates","results"}` with one
215	`{"series_id","written","duplicates"}` per entry in input order; the totals
216	are the per-entry sums. A successful batch with `written > 0` increases
217	`stats()["writes"]` by exactly one; a pure-duplicate batch increases nothing.
218	Quotas are charged per tenant with the batch's net new series and distinct new
219	timestamps — duplicates and overwrites add no occupancy, and only dimensions
220	that actually increase are checked. Any rejection (structure, missing fields,
221	per-entry validation, future samples → `400`; conflict or quota → `409`)
222	leaves no series, sample or write-count change behind, on disk included, and
223	concurrent queries and quota reads only ever see the state before or after the
224	whole batch. Replaying the same batch re-judges duplicates and overwrites in
225	the same order.
226	
227	**Snapshot export and replay.** `export_snapshot(tenant, metric, labels=None,
228	start_ms=None, end_ms=None, matchers=None)` (also `GET /v1/export` and the CLI
229	`export`) captures the raw samples of every matching series as a verifiable
230	document `{"version": 1, "snapshot_id": ..., "entries": [...]}`. The filters
231	and the closed `[start_ms, end_ms]` interval behave exactly as in `query`.
232	Each entry holds only `tenant`, `metric`, `labels` and `samples` (ascending by
233	timestamp); entries are ordered by `series_id` and registered series with no
234	sample in range are omitted. `snapshot_id` is the SHA-256 of the sorted,
235	compact JSON UTF-8 bytes of `{"version": 1, "entries": [...]}`. The export
236	reads one coherent snapshot under a single lock acquisition and never changes
237	write counters, quotas, alerts or query results, so exporting the same state
238	twice yields identical content.
239	
240	`replay_snapshot(snapshot, now_ms=None, overwrite=False, dry_run=False)` (also
241	`POST /v1/replay` and the CLI `replay --snapshot '<json>'`) verifies the
242	document before storing anything: the version must be 1, `snapshot_id` must
243	match the entries digest, and every entry then goes through the `write_batch`
244	rules (labels, samples, future timestamps against `now_ms` when given,
245	conflicts, per-tenant quotas). Invalid input or a digest mismatch is a `400`,
246	a conflict or quota breach a `409`, and any failure leaves no in-memory or
247	on-disk change behind. The result is `{"written", "duplicates", "results",
248	"applied"}` with `results` in entry order. A dry run (`dry_run=true` /
249	`--dry-run`) performs all validation and counting but applies nothing and
250	reports `applied: false`; a real replay reports `applied: true` (`202` over
251	HTTP, `200` for a dry run). Replaying a snapshot onto the state it came from
252	is a pure duplicate replay (`written == 0`, the write counter does not move),
253	replaying onto a partial state fills in only the missing points, and a replay
254	after a restart re-judges exactly as an in-process one. Replay never mints new
255	series identities and does not alter labels, tenant isolation, query
256	aggregation, alert or SLO semantics. With access control enabled, export is a
257	`read` operation scoped to the requested tenant and replay is a `write`
258	operation checked per entry — any entry outside the caller's scope rejects the
259	whole replay with `403` — and both are audited like every other endpoint.
260	
261	**Bucketing.** `query(..., step_ms=step, agg=agg)` assigns a sample with
262	timestamp `t` to bucket `b = t - (t % step)`, i.e. buckets are
263	left-closed/right-open (`[b, b+step)`) on epoch multiples. Every bucket from the
264	first non-empty bucket to the last non-empty bucket that also lies inside
265	`[start_ms, end_ms]` is emitted, and buckets with no sample are emitted as
266	`[b, null]`. Bucket value = `agg` over the samples in the bucket, where `agg` is
267	one of `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`. A series whose range contains no
268	sample is still listed with an empty `points` list. With `agg` and *no*
269	`step_ms` the whole `[start_ms, end_ms]` range is a single bucket. With neither,
270	raw samples are returned in `[timestamp, value]` order. `rollup(tenant, metric,
271	labels, window_ms, agg)` is `query` with `step_ms = window_ms` over the whole
272	stored range, with empty buckets dropped; output is ordered by `series_id`, so
273	it is deterministic.
274	
275	**Label matchers.** In addition to exact `labels` / `label.k=v` filtering,
276	`query` accepts `matchers` (`matchers` on `GET /v1/query`, `--matchers` on the
277	CLI): a JSON array of objects containing exactly `key` (non-empty string),
278	`op` and `value` (string, may be empty). Ops are `=` / `!=` (exact whole-string
279	equality and negation) and `=~` / `!~` (Python `re` syntax matched against the
280	*whole* label value via full match, case-sensitive and Unicode-aware, and its
281	negation). Omitting the parameter, passing Python `None`, or sending `[]` adds
282	no condition; an explicit JSON `null` or empty text is rejected (HTTP/CLI).
283	Matchers combine with each other and with the exact label filters by logical
284	AND — including several matchers on the same key — apply to raw series labels
285	before bucketing or grouping (labels absent from `group_by` count too), and are
286	restricted to the requested `tenant` and `metric`; `tenant`, `metric` and
287	`series_id` are not implicit labels. A missing key never satisfies `=`/`=~` but
288	always satisfies `!=`/`!~`, so `=~ ""` selects only series where the key exists
289	with an empty value (grouping still separates a missing key from an empty
290	value). `api-.*` matches `api-a` but not `xapi-a`. Duplicate matchers never
291	duplicate series, matcher order is irrelevant, and contradictory matchers
292	yield an empty result. Invalid JSON, a non-array, non-object elements, missing
293	or extra fields, wrong types, an empty `key`, an unsupported `op` or an invalid
294	regex raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON error line on stderr for the
295	CLI); every matcher is validated even when no candidate series exists.
296	
297	**Grouped query.** `query(..., agg=agg, group_by=[keys...])` aggregates *across*
298	series: matching series (same tenant/metric/label filters and `[start_ms,
299	end_ms]` range as above) are bucketed into groups by the values of the given
300	label keys, and the raw in-range samples of all series in a group are pooled
301	before `agg` is applied — samples from different series at the same timestamp
302	count individually. `group_by=[]` merges every matching series into one group.
303	Each result row carries only `labels` (the group keys actually present on the
304	group's series — a missing key and an empty-string value form different
305	groups) and `points`; rows are ordered lexicographically by their sorted label
306	pairs. Bucketing follows the same rules as the per-series query (epoch-aligned
307	left-closed buckets with `null` gaps, or a single point at the group's
308	earliest sample without `step_ms`). A group whose series have no sample in
309	range is still listed with empty `points`; no matching series at all yields an
310	empty `series` array. `group_by` must be a list of distinct non-empty strings
311	and requires `agg`; violations raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON
312	error line on stderr for the CLI).
313	
314	**Sliding-window query.** `query(..., start_ms=start, end_ms=end, step_ms=step,
315	agg=agg, window_ms=window)` switches to a separate mode the moment `window_ms`
316	is supplied (it is optional in every binding: `window` on `GET /v1/query`,
317	`--window-ms` on the CLI). In this mode `start_ms`, `end_ms`, `step_ms` and
318	`agg` are all required; `start_ms` and `end_ms` must be integer milliseconds,
319	`step_ms` and `window_ms` positive integer milliseconds, and `end_ms >=
320	start_ms` (bools, fractions and missing/unknown values are rejected). Evaluation
321	times are `t = start + k*step` for `k = 0, 1, ...`, keeping only times
322	`t <= end`; the output point timestamp is the evaluation time itself. The step
323	need not divide the window and windows are never aligned to fixed buckets.
324	
325	Each evaluation aggregates the raw samples in the half-open interval
326	`(t - window_ms, t]`: the left edge is excluded (a sample exactly one window
327	length earlier does not count), the right edge included (a sample at `t`
328	does). `start_ms` only constrains the output grid — the first window at
329	`start` also reads history older than `start`; no window ever reads a sample
330	newer than its own evaluation time. The aggregation uses the same meanings as
331	bucketing (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`), and a window containing no
332	sample emits `[t, null]` for *every* aggregation, including `count`.
333	
334	Every matching registered series is returned on the full time grid even when
335	all of its windows are empty; no matching series yields an empty `series`
336	array. The Python per-series rows keep `series_id`; HTTP and CLI keep the
337	existing result shape. With `group_by`, all raw samples of the group's series
338	that fall in each window are pooled before aggregating (samples sharing a
339	timestamp across series count individually, `avg` divides by the total sample
340	count), a missing group key and an empty-string value stay distinct groups,
341	and each group keeps the full grid, fully null when no sample ever falls in a
342	window. Group filtering, ordering and validation follow the ordinary grouped
343	rules. The whole query reads one coherent snapshot, so concurrent writes or
344	retention sweeps can never mix old and new data; queries never alter samples,
345	counters or configuration, and the same history gives identical results after
346	reopening the store. Omitting `window_ms` preserves the previous query
347	behaviour exactly — `rollup`, write idempotency/overwrite, quotas, alerts and
348	SLOs are unaffected.
349	
350	**Counter aggregates.** In sliding-window mode `agg` also accepts `increase`
351	and `rate` (query entries only — `rollup`, alert rules and SLOs still reject
352	them, and using them without `window_ms` fails the query). Each matching
353	series is treated as a counter: within `(t - window_ms, t]` the time-sorted
354	adjacent readings contribute their difference when non-decreasing, while a
355	drop is a counter reset contributing only the later reading; the first reading
356	contributes nothing. Only samples actually inside the window are used — no
357	boundary borrowing, interpolation or extrapolation by window length.
358	`increase` is the sum of those deltas, `rate` that sum divided by the seconds
359	between the window's first and last sample. A window with fewer than two
360	distinct sample timestamps emits `[t, null]`; unchanged readings emit `0`.
361	Grouped queries compute each series independently and sum the non-null
362	per-series results (never differencing across series); a group whose series
363	are all null at a time emits null there. Any matched sample that actually
364	falls into an output window and is negative or non-finite fails the whole
365	query (`ObsError`, HTTP `400`, CLI non-zero with a one-line JSON error);
366	samples outside every window or filtered out by labels/matchers are never
367	inspected, and parameters are validated even when no series matches.
368	
369	**Retention.** `enforce_retention(tenant, cutoff_ms)` removes every sample of
370	that tenant with `timestamp_millis < cutoff_ms` and rewrites the affected point
371	files. `stats()` returns `{"series","points","writes","tenants"}`.
372	
373	**Retention policies and runs.** `set_retention(tenant, retention_ms)`
374	persists the tenant's policy in `retention.json` (also `POST
375	/v1/retention/policies` and the CLI `retention-set`); `retention_ms` is a
376	non-negative integer or `null` (no cleanup), and `get_retention(tenant)`
377	(also `GET /v1/retention/policies` and `retention-get`) returns
378	`{"tenant","retention_ms","series","points"}` — the normalised policy plus the
379	tenant's real usage, with a `null` policy for unconfigured tenants.
380	`run_retention(now_ms, tenant=None, dry_run=False)` (also `POST
381	/v1/retention/run` and `retention-run`) applies the configured policies as of
382	the injected `now_ms` (a required non-boolean integer): with a `tenant` only
383	that tenant is processed, otherwise every configured tenant in lexicographic
384	order. For each tenant `cutoff_ms = now_ms - retention_ms` and only samples
385	with `timestamp_ms < cutoff_ms` are dropped — a sample exactly at the cutoff
386	is kept; a `null` policy reports a `null` cutoff and zero deletions. Affected
387	point files are rewritten in compacted form (one physical record per
388	timestamp, the final value winning, legacy duplicate lines collapsed), empty
389	series stay registered, and the freed points count against the tenant's quota
390	immediately. The result is `{"dry_run","tenants":[...]}` with a stable
391	tenant order and `{"tenant","cutoff_ms","dropped","affected_series",
392	"remaining_points","compacted_series"}` per tenant. The whole run is one
393	atomic step under the store lock, so concurrent queries, quota and stats reads
394	only ever see the complete state before or after it; `dry_run=true` reports
395	the same numbers without touching memory, files, quotas or the write counter.
396	Policies and sweep results survive a restart. With access control enabled,
397	reading a policy is a tenant-scoped `read`, setting a policy and running a
398	single-tenant sweep are tenant-scoped `write`s, a sweep across every
399	configured tenant is admin-only, and all of them are audited.
400	
401	**Persistent downsampling.** `set_downsampling_policy(tenant, metric, step_ms,
402	aggregations)` (also `POST /v1/downsampling/policies` and the CLI
403	`downsampling-set`) creates or replaces the per-(tenant, metric) policy:
404	`step_ms` is a positive integer bucket resolution and `aggregations` a
405	non-empty list of distinct entries from `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`;
406	anything else is rejected with `downsampling policy invalid` (`400`) and
407	leaves the persisted config untouched. Replacing a policy keeps the raw
408	samples but clears the previously computed results of that (tenant, metric).
409	`get_downsampling_policy(tenant, metric)` (also `GET
410	/v1/downsampling/policies` and `downsampling-get`) returns the normalised
411	policy, with `null` fields when unconfigured.
412	
413	`run_downsampling(now_ms, tenant=None, metric=None, dry_run=False)` (also
414	`POST /v1/downsampling/run` and `downsampling-run`) recomputes persisted
415	buckets from the raw samples with `timestamp_ms <= now_ms` (`now_ms` is a
416	required non-boolean integer; any invalid argument is `downsampling run
417	invalid`, `400`). With `tenant`/`metric` given only the matching policies
418	run, otherwise every configured policy runs in (tenant, metric) order.
419	Bucketing uses the same epoch-aligned left-closed buckets and aggregation
420	meanings as `query`; every bucket holding at least one processed sample is
421	recomputed for each declared aggregation, so a repeated run recomputes
422	exactly the affected buckets while buckets whose raw samples were cleaned by
423	retention keep their stored values — retention only ever drops raw points.
424	The result is `{"dry_run","policies":[{"tenant","metric","buckets",
425	"changed"},...]}` (`buckets` recomputed, `changed` actually differing). A dry
426	run changes neither data nor the revision; a real run is one atomic commit
427	and increases the persistent revision exactly once when at least one bucket
428	changed. Results are persisted under `downsampled/` and survive restarts.
429	
430	`query_downsampled(tenant, metric, ...)` (also `GET /v1/query/downsampled`
431	and `downsampled-query`) reads the persisted buckets with the step fixed to
432	the policy's `step_ms` and the same interval, bucket-start, null-filled empty
433	bucket, ordering and matcher semantics as `query`. With no policy configured
434	the read fails with `downsampling policy unavailable` (`404`); an `agg` the
435	policy does not declare fails with `downsampling aggregation unavailable`
436	(`400`); sliding windows, grouping and the counter aggregates are
437	`downsampled query unsupported` (`400`). `read_token` reuses the ordinary
438	read-consistency errors. With access control enabled the downsampled read is
439	a tenant-scoped `read`, policy modification and a single-tenant run are
440	tenant-scoped `write`s, a run across every configured policy is admin-only,
441	and all of them are audited; raw write/query behaviour is unchanged.
442	
443	**Per-tenant quotas.** `set_quota(tenant, max_series, max_points)` sets the
444	tenant-wide limits; each limit is a non-negative integer or `null` (omitted
445	fields over HTTP also mean `null`, i.e. unlimited), and `0` forbids adding any.
446	`get_quota(tenant)` returns
447	`{"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` — the configured
448	limits and the current usage in one snapshot. Configuring a quota never creates
449	a series, and an unconfigured tenant is unlimited. Limits apply to all of a
450	tenant's metrics together: `series` is the number of registered series and
451	`points` the total number of *distinct timestamps* across those series, not
452	physical point-file lines. Label order, same-value replays, overwritten points
453	and a timestamp repeated inside one batch add no occupancy.
454	
455	Every write path (`SeriesStore.write`/`write_batch`, `POST /v1/series` and
456	`/v1/series/batch`, the CLI `write`/`write-batch`) is
457	checked after the existing input validation and conflict rules, using the
458	batch's net increase: a batch is rejected (ObsError / HTTP `409` / CLI JSON
459	error with non-zero exit) when *either* dimension it increases would exceed its
460	limit, and the rejection leaves no new series, samples or write-count change.
461	Limits may be lowered below current usage; afterwards only the dimensions a
462	write actually increases are checked — an already-over-limit dimension blocks
463	nothing by itself, so pure duplicates and overwrites keep succeeding. Retention
464	frees the occupancy of deleted points, while empty series stay registered.
465	Overwrites rewrite the point file so one timestamp never occupies two lines; on
466	reopen, any duplicate timestamp lines (including those left by older builds)
467	collapse to the last value, so historical re-overwrites never double-count.
468	
469	**Rule shape.** `{"id","tenant","metric","labels","comparator" ∈ {">",">=","<",
470	"<=","==","!="},"threshold","for_ms","window_ms","agg","severity" ∈ {"info",
471	"warning","critical"},"annotations"}`. `add_rule` validates every field and
472	raises `ObsError` for anything malformed (`id` is generated when omitted).
473	
474	**Evaluation window.** Let `step = window_ms`, `t = now_ms` and
475	`bucket_start(t) = t - (t % step)`. The window is
476	`[bucket_start(t) - step, t]`, i.e. the current bucket plus the whole previous
477	bucket. The rule condition holds for a series when *every* non-empty bucket in
478	that window satisfies `comparator(value, threshold)` — one violating bucket
479	anywhere in the window stops the condition, and it keeps stopping it until that
480	bucket has left the window.
481	
482	**`for_ms`.** Let `run_start` be the timestamp of the first bucket of the
483	current unbroken run of satisfying buckets (a violating bucket resets the run).
484	The rule fires only when the condition holds *and*
485	`bucket_start(now_ms) - run_start >= for_ms`. With `for_ms = 0`, one satisfied
486	bucket is enough; with `for_ms = window_ms`, the current and the previous bucket
487	must both be satisfied. Before the hold time is reached the alert is recorded
488	with `firing = false` and appears in none of the four output lists.
489	
490	**Alert identity and dedup.** Alert identity is `(rule_id, series_id)`, distinct
491	from the alert id. The first time a condition holds an alert id
492	`alert-NNNNN` is minted for that identity and reused forever: re-evaluating an
493	unchanged condition returns the *same* `id` and increments `occurrences` (the
494	number of evaluations in which the condition held). `since_ms` is `run_start`,
495	not the evaluation time, so dedup does not depend on the wall clock.
496	
497	**Resolution.** When the condition stops holding, the alert's state becomes
498	`resolved`, `firing` becomes `false`, `resolved_ms` is set once, and the alert is
499	reported in the `resolved` list of that evaluation. If the same condition holds
500	again later, the *same alert id* is reused and `occurrences` keeps counting.
501	Because the condition covers the whole window, a series that produced one bad
502	bucket stays unresolved until that bucket has left the window.
503	
504	**Silence vs inhibition precedence.** A condition that holds and whose `for_ms`
505	is satisfied is first checked against active silences: a silence is active when
506	`starts_ms <= now_ms <= ends_ms`, the tenant matches and every silence label
507	matcher is present in the series labels. Inside an active silence the alert state
508	is `silenced` (it is *not* firing) and the silence id and reason are recorded.
509	Only if no silence matches is inhibition checked: an inhibition
510	`(source_severity, target_severity, same_labels)` marks a `target_severity` alert
511	as `inhibited` while an alert of at least `source_severity` is currently
512	`firing` in the same tenant with *exactly the same label set*. Silence therefore
513	wins over inhibition. A silenced or inhibited alert still counts its
514	`occurrences` and returns to `firing` as soon as the silence/inhibition no longer
515	applies. `list_alerts(state=None)` filters by `firing`, `silenced`, `inhibited`
516	or `resolved`.
517	
518	**Notification routing.** `add_route({"tenant","target","labels"?,"severities"?,
519	"events"?,"repeat_ms"?,"id"?})` registers a notification route; `tenant` and
520	`target` are required non-empty strings, `labels` is an exact label subset the
521	alert's series must contain, `severities` (default: all severities) and
522	`events` (default: `["firing","resolved"]`, the only two allowed values) are
523	non-empty arrays when given, and `repeat_ms` is `null` or a non-negative
524	integer. Invalid shapes raise `ObsError` (HTTP `400`), a duplicate `id` is a
525	conflict (HTTP `409`), an unknown route is `404`; without an `id` the route is
526	named `route-NNNN`. Deleting a route keeps its historical notifications.
527	
528	`evaluate(now_ms)` still returns only the four state lists, but every alert
529	transition also appends to the notification queue of each matching route
530	(tenant equal, route labels a subset of the series labels, alert severity in
531	`severities`): an alert that enters `firing` — the first time, or when
532	recovering from `silenced`/`inhibited` — produces one `firing` record; while
533	the same firing state continues a repeat is emitted only when `repeat_ms` is
534	set and that much time has passed since the route's last notification for the
535	alert; entering `resolved` produces exactly one `resolved` record. Pending
536	(`for_ms` not yet met), silenced and inhibited alerts never produce `firing`
537	records. Dedup is tracked per route, so routes notify independently. Each
538	record is `{"id": "notification-NNNNN","route_id","alert_id","tenant",
539	"target","event","created_ms","alert": <snapshot>,"acked": false}` and is
540	persisted across restarts together with the dedup state.
541	`list_notifications(tenant, route_id, alert_id, acked)` reads the queue
542	without consuming it; `ack_notification(id)` marks a record acknowledged,
543	returns the same record on a repeated ack and raises `ObsError` (HTTP `404`)
544	for an unknown id.
545	
546	**SLO and error budget.** `set_slo(tenant, name, metric, labels,
547	good_comparator, threshold, target_ratio, window_ms)` defines a good-events
548	ratio SLO. `slo_status(name, now_ms, tenant=None)` counts every stored sample of
549	the matching series inside `[now_ms - window_ms, now_ms]`:
550	
551	```
552	total          = number of samples in the window (nulls excluded)
553	good           = samples where compare(value, good_comparator, threshold)
554	bad            = total - good
555	ratio          = good / total                             (0.0 when total == 0)
556	error_budget   = max(0.0, 1 - (1 - ratio) / (1 - target_ratio))   (target_ratio < 1)
557	               = 1.0 if ratio >= 1.0 else 0.0              (target_ratio == 1)
558	burn_rate      = (bad / total) / (1 - target_ratio)        (0.0 when target_ratio >= 1 or total == 0)
559	met            = ratio >= target_ratio
560	```
561	
562	`ratio` is the observed good ratio, `target_ratio ∈ (0,1]` the objective,
563	`burn_rate` how fast the budget is being spent relative to the allowed bad rate
564	(`1.0` means exactly on budget, `> 1.0` means burning too fast) and
565	`error_budget` the *fraction of the allowed error budget still unspent*:
566	`1.0` means untouched, `0.0` means exhausted or exceeded. For any `ratio` that
567	meets the target the two written forms of `error_budget` are identical, since
568	`1 - (1-ratio)/(1-target) = (ratio - target)/(1 - target)` and
569	`1 - ratio/target = (target - ratio)/target` are both non-negative only inside
570	their own regime; the first form is the one used, because it degrades sensibly
571	when the ratio beats the target (more budget left) instead of pinning to `0`.
572	With `total == 0` the ratio is `0.0`, so the budget counts as exhausted.
573	
574	Examples: 9 good + 1 bad with `target_ratio = 0.9` gives `ratio = 0.9`,
575	`error_budget = 0.0`, `burn_rate = 0.1/0.1 = 1.0`, `met = true` (exactly on
576	budget). 98 good + 2 bad with `target_ratio = 0.95` gives `ratio = 0.98`,
577	`burn_rate = 0.02/0.05 = 0.4` and `error_budget = 1 - 0.02/0.05 = 0.6` (60% of
578	the budget still unspent). 90 good + 10 bad with `target_ratio = 0.99` gives
579	`ratio = 0.9`, `burn_rate = 10.0`, `error_budget = 0.0`, `met = false`.
580	
581	**Revisions and read consistency.** The store keeps one persistent,
582	monotonically increasing *revision* in `revision.json`. Every successful
583	commit that changes samples or the visible scope — a single write, a batch
584	write, a snapshot replay or a retention run that actually drops samples —
585	increases it exactly once. Pure duplicates, dry runs, validation failures,
586	conflicts, quota rejections and retention runs that delete nothing do not
587	move it, and neither do queries, exports or SLO status reads. The counter is
588	reloaded on construction (and folded in from disk on demand), so numbering
589	continues across restarts and stays monotonic when several instances share
590	one data dir; a failed batch or replay leaves neither data nor a revision
591	trace, and concurrent queries and retention sweeps only ever see the
592	complete state before or after a commit.
593	
594	`consistency_token(tenant)` (also `GET /v1/consistency-token?tenant=` and
595	the CLI `consistency-token`) returns `{"tenant", "token", "revision"}`: an
596	HMAC-signed cursor binding the tenant to the current revision. The signing
597	secret is persisted in `revision.json`, so tokens stay verifiable after a
598	restart and across instances of the same data dir.
599	
600	The write paths accept an optional `return_revision` flag (`return_revision`
601	in the HTTP bodies, `--return-revision` on the CLI `write`, `write-batch`,
602	`replay` and `retention-run`). It must be a real boolean — an explicit
603	`null` or any other type is rejected with `400` semantics before anything
604	changes. When enabled, the result (Python dict, HTTP JSON or CLI one-line
605	JSON) carries an extra `revision`: the commit revision when the call
606	committed, otherwise the current revision. When omitted, results keep their
607	previous shape exactly.
608	
609	`query`, `export_snapshot` and `slo_status` accept an optional `read_token`
610	(`read_token` on `GET /v1/query`, `/v1/export` and `/v1/slos/status`,
611	`--read-token` on the CLI). A read carrying a token is gated on the token's
612	revision: it is processed only once this instance has caught up to it, and
613	then runs on one coherent snapshot. Re-reading with the same token may see
614	newer data but never older. A tampered, malformed, foreign or cross-tenant
615	token fails with `invalid read token` (`400`); a token whose revision the
616	instance has not reached yet fails with `read revision unavailable` (`409`).
617	The consistency-token endpoint is an ordinary tenant-scoped read: with
618	access control enabled only a principal covering the tenant can mint or use
619	its tokens, and every request is audited as usual; while no `access.json`
620	exists everything stays anonymous.
621	
622	**Determinism.** No module calls `time.time()` inside decision logic: `now_ms` is
623	passed into `evaluate`, `slo_status` and `write` (the HTTP layer uses the wall
624	clock only when a caller omits `now_ms` on `GET /v1/slos/status`, and
625	`/v1/slos/status` requires it in the CLI).
626	
627	## Layout
628	
629	```
630	obsd/__init__.py    public exports
631	obsd/tsdb.py        SeriesStore
632	obsd/alerts.py      AlertEngine
633	obsd/access.py      AccessControl (principals + audit log)
634	obsd/http_app.py    ThreadingHTTPServer + create_server
635	obsd/cli.py         command line interface
636	obsd/__main__.py    python3 -m obsd entry point
637	tests/              unittest suite (tsdb, alerts, http, access)
638	```
639	
640	## Tests
641	
642	```bash
643	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
644	```
645	
646	Covered: series identity and label-order independence, idempotent re-write,
647	conflicting-timestamp rejection and `overwrite`, range filtering, epoch-aligned
648	buckets, null buckets, all five aggregations, deterministic rollups,
649	sliding-window grids with left-open/right-closed windows, null empty windows
650	(including count), full grids for empty series and groups, window argument
651	validation across Python/HTTP/CLI, window snapshot consistency under
652	concurrent writes and retention, retention,
653	restart safety, rule validation, `for_ms` timing, dedup with occurrence
654	counting, resolution and re-firing (including the window that keeps a bad bucket
655	blocking), silence scoping and expiry, inhibition by severity and exact label
656	set, SLO/error-budget/burn-rate math (including the empty window), quota
657	configuration/validation, net-increase enforcement and whole-batch rejection,
658	zero/lowered limits with duplicates and overwrites, tenant isolation, quota
659	release under retention, quota/usage consistency after reopen (including
660	collapsed duplicate timestamp lines), concurrent writes/reconfiguration/pruning,
661	retention policy set/get/validation and persistence, retention runs (exclusive
662	cutoff with the boundary point kept, lexicographic all-tenant sweeps, null
663	policies, dry runs without side effects, physical compaction of duplicate
664	timestamps, empty series staying registered, freed points reusable under quota,
665	restart-stable results, whole-state visibility under concurrent reads, and the
666	HTTP/CLI surfaces with tenant-scoped and admin-only access plus audit),
667	atomic multi-series batches (cross-tenant/cross-metric entries, in-batch
668	duplicate/overwrite ordering, all-or-nothing rejection on disk, per-tenant net
669	quota accounting, single write-count increment, and the HTTP/CLI surfaces),
670	principal create/list/revoke with digest-only token persistence, role and
671	tenant-scope enforcement (`401`/`403`) with the anonymous surface unchanged
672	while access control is off, per-entry batch authorization with atomic
673	rejection, the persistent audit log (seq monotonic across restarts, filters
674	and `limit` pagination on `GET /v1/audit`),
675	verifiable snapshot export (filters, ordering, digest, side-effect-free
676	repeatability across restarts) and replay (roundtrip migration, duplicate and
677	missing-point re-judgement, dry runs, digest/validation/conflict/quota
678	rejection without a trace, per-entry authorization, and the HTTP/CLI
679	surfaces),
680	the persistent revision (single increments per committing write/batch/replay/
681	retention run, no movement on duplicates, dry runs, rejections or reads,
682	restart and multi-instance continuity) with `return_revision` on every write
683	path, and read-consistency tokens (minting, tamper/cross-tenant/foreign
684	rejection, unavailable-revision `409`s, monotonic re-reads, restart
685	verifiability, and the HTTP/CLI surfaces with access control and audit),
686	persistent downsampling (policy set/get/validation and persistence,
687	replacement clearing results but keeping raw samples, runs with epoch-bucket
688	recomputation, dry runs, single revision bumps, tenant/metric filtering,
689	restart and retention survival, downsampled queries with null-filled buckets,
690	matcher/label filtering, the unavailable/unsupported error shapes, and the
691	HTTP/CLI surfaces with role scoping and audit),
692	and the live HTTP surface over a real socket.
693	
694	Everything is deterministic: the suite injects every timestamp it uses, and the
695	modules never read the wall clock inside decision logic.
696
